newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Week closes with KEB.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DEBT MARKETS - Week closes with KEB.

text.p: Korea Exchange Bank slipped in with a US$100 million floating rate note issue launched in London, the only launch in a slow Asian debt day Friday.
The one-year FRN was launched at par and re-offered at 99.975 to float at 20 basis points over the three-month London Interbank Offered Rate. Fees are five basis points.
Fuji International Finance was the lead.
One-year issues have become popular among Korean borrowers on the view that they will be able to finance at better terms next year if South Korea joins the OECD by end-1996, as is expected.
In Hong Kong, Yang Zi Lin, chief executive of the Hong Kong and Macau regional offices of the Bank of China, said he expects the bank's debut Hong Kong dollar debt issue to be extremely successful.

Yang said that at least half of the 40 banks contacted by Bank of China already have expressed interest in joining the facility and that he believed all of the banks approached eventually would commit to the deal.
Bank of China group member China Development Finance Co will arrange the HK$2 billion five-year FRCD for Bank of China.

Yang confirmed speculation that the certificates would pay an all-in return of about 40 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate, comparable to that paid by similar bank issues in the territory.
Earlier today, sources at CDFC confirmed that Bank of China issue had received approval from China's State Administration of Exchange Control (SAEC).

In other news from Hong Kong, Chase Manhattan Asia, HSBC Investment Bank Asia and J.P. Morgan Securities Asia announced that they have been mandated to arrange a HK$3.5 billion equivalent term loan facility for Hong Kong's CITIC Pacific.

As for deals already done, arrangers of Wheelock's revolving credit/term loan facility said that the deal had been increased to HK$5 billion from HK$4.5 billion after being oversubscribed in general syndication.
The facility already had been increased from HK$3 billion in the sub-underwriting phase.

In other loan news, Banco Santander, J.P. Morgan Securities Asia, KEB Asia Finance, Sakura Bank, ST Capital and Union Bank of Switzerland said they would arrange a US$115 million project-related loan to fund a bridges and tunnel project in China's Guangdong province.

In the capital markets, lead manager Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said it was pleased with the market response to the US$200 million floating rate note issue of General Housing Bank of Thailand, a DMG source said.
The housing bank FRN, launched Thursday in London, replaced Thailand's sovereign FRN issue.
DMG sold US$11 million more than its US$114 million allotment and bought some of the co-managers' share. The issue was placed with institutional investors in Europe and Asia.
Other bankers said they expected most of the housing bank issue to end up in Asia.
Sources close to Malaysia's state-owned oil company Petronas today said the company plans to issue a Yankee bond later this month or in early October.
CS First Boston and Salomon Brothers have been appointed joint lead managers, the source said.
